What We Do

Full-Service Telehealth Revenue Cycle Management

Telehealth billing requires payer-by-payer telehealth coverage verification, correct modifier and place of service code application, audio-only vs. audio-visual distinction, and state licensure confirmation for cross-state visits. PMEX manages every layer so telehealth revenue is captured correctly on every encounter.

Modifier 95 Application

Synchronous telehealth modifier 95 applied on every qualifying telehealth visit.

Place of Service Coding

POS 02 (telehealth, other than home) and POS 10 (patient home) applied per patient location.

Audio-Only Billing

Audio-only telephone visit codes (99441 to 99443) billed when video is not used.

Payer Coverage Verification

Telehealth coverage confirmed per payer per CPT code before every visit is scheduled.

State Licensure Tracking

Provider licensure verified in the patient state before cross-state telehealth visits are billed.

Medicare Telehealth Compliance

Medicare telehealth originating site and distant site requirements applied per visit type.

Sound Familiar?

Common Telehealth Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Telehealth visit billed with office POS (11) instead of POS 02 or 10, adjudicated at wrong rate.

PMEX applies POS 02 or POS 10 per the patient location on every telehealth visit.

Modifier 95 missing on telehealth E/M claims, triggering payer edit failures.

PMEX applies modifier 95 to every synchronous audio-visual telehealth visit before submission.

Audio-only visit billed with video telehealth codes instead of telephone codes.

PMEX confirms visit modality before coding: audio-visual visits use modifier 95, audio-only visits use 99441 to 99443.

Cross-state telehealth visit billed without confirming provider licensure in the patient state.

PMEX verifies provider licensure in the patient state before the visit is billed.

Payer-specific telehealth CPT code restrictions not checked, submitting non-covered codes.

PMEX verifies payer telehealth coverage per CPT code before each visit type is scheduled and billed.

Medicare telehealth originating site fee not billed for qualifying rural patient locations.

PMEX confirms originating site eligibility and submits Q3014 for qualifying Medicare rural telehealth visits.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Telehealth Billing

Telehealth practices lose 18 to 30 percent of revenue to place of service errors, missing modifiers, and payer coverage verification gaps.

PATTERN 01

Telehealth Visit Denied, Wrong Place of Service Applied

Telehealth visit submitted with POS 11 (office). Payer adjudicates at the office rate but flags the visit for review. On review: patient was at home. POS 10 (patient home) was required. Claim adjusted downward or denied for incorrect POS.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms the patient location at the time of every telehealth visit and applies the correct place of service code: POS 02 for telehealth at a location other than home, POS 10 when the patient is at home.

PATTERN 02

Audio-Only Visit Billed with Wrong Telehealth Codes

Provider conducts a telephone-only visit. 99213 with modifier 95 submitted. Modifier 95 requires two-way audio-visual communication. Audio-only visits require 99441 to 99443 (telephone E/M codes). Payer denies modifier 95 for audio-only visit.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms visit modality before billing. Synchronous audio-visual visits use E/M codes with modifier 95. Audio-only telephone visits use the 99441 to 99443 telephone code series per the visit duration.

PATTERN 03

Cross-State Telehealth Visit Denied, Provider Not Licensed in Patient State

Provider licensed in New York delivers a telehealth visit to a patient located in Florida. Claim submitted. Florida payer denies: provider not licensed in Florida. Revenue lost. Compliance exposure created for the unlicensed practice of medicine.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX verifies provider licensure in the patient state before cross-state telehealth visits are scheduled. Visits in states where the provider is not licensed are flagged before the appointment is confirmed.

Questions

Telehealth Billing Questions Answered

Modifier 95 (synchronous telehealth) is the current CMS-required modifier for telehealth services. Modifier GT (via interactive audio and video telecommunications) was the prior modifier and may still apply on some payer contracts. We apply the correct modifier per payer.

POS 02 is used when the patient is at a healthcare facility or other non-home location for the telehealth visit. POS 10 is used when the patient is at their home. The correct POS affects the fee schedule applied by Medicare and many commercial payers.

Telephone visits without audio-visual capability are billed with CPT 99441 (5 to 10 minutes), 99442 (11 to 20 minutes), or 99443 (21 to 30 minutes) based on the documented duration of the medical discussion.

No. Each payer has a list of approved telehealth CPT codes. We verify payer coverage per CPT code before scheduling visits and avoid billing non-covered codes via telehealth.

We verify provider licensure in the patient state before any cross-state visit is billed. Interstate licensure compact participation is tracked per provider, and non-compact states require individual licensure verification.

Within 30 days, with payer telehealth coverage matrices verified and modifier workflows active from day one.
